neighbours.label: a magnitude word (amount, number, levels, close, low) under an extreme intensifier ('a record number', 'dangerously close', 'unbearably low'), versus the same word with a neutral modifier
fire: The river rose perilously close to the top of the levee.
Fans spent an insane amount of money on tickets this summer.
An all-time record number of students applied to the college.
Tests found toxic levels of lead in the old water pipes.
Nurses complained about shockingly low pay at the clinic.
We ate a ridiculous amount of cake at the wedding.
Workers were exposed to dangerous levels of noise in the mill.
The team came agonizingly close to winning the title.
quiet: The river rose close to the top of the levee by morning.
Fans spent a fair amount of money on tickets this summer.
A large share of the students applied to the college.
Tests found traces of lead in the old water pipes.
Nurses talked about the pay at the clinic during lunch.
We ate a slice of cake at the wedding.
Workers checked the levels of oil in the machines at the mill.
The team came back home after the final game.

predictions: fire 0.6-0.95 on the magnitude word after an extreme intensifier; the same word with neutral or no modifier below 0.03
notes: Card (max 23): 'dangerously close', 'mind-boggling amount', 'record number', 'hazardous levels', 'crazy amount', 'unbearably low'.
